result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers read the stall well: no decision owner, no date and no cost put on the problem. Both suggest sizing fuel and overtime in the buyer's own numbers. B wins mainly on rubric item 4: its closing email gives a clear point to stop spending effort, while A only implies one ('if she won't pick a date'). A also has a stray 'as the skill suggests' line that makes no sense to this user. A is a bit stronger on item 5, the concrete lesson of getting the figures before the demo and holding the quote until the signer is known. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B reads the silence more rigorously: it separates what is known from what isn't, ties the stall to the missing sized business case and the missing signer, and gives a sharper lesson for next time (get the cost numbers before the demo, and don't quote until someone has said who signs and when). A is solid and has a clearer stopping point in its closing email, but its reading of the silence is shallower and its lesson is thinner. B has a stray 'as the skill suggests' line, which is a small polish flaw.
